gold.gold_rationale: Clause 12(5) conditions breach on explicit consent (breach -> consent). 1500-B-LOOKUP-ACCT rejects any transaction that would exceed ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT (lines 403-411) and the main loop never posts a failed transaction (lines 211-216), making the antecedent always false and the conditional vacuously satisfied, per the adjudication note.

provenance.annotator_notes: Adjudicated 2026-07-27: Pass 1 read the blanket rejection of over-limit transactions as conformant (D7); Pass 2 read the absent consent-capture path as a missing rule (D2). Resolved on the clause's own grammar: 'shall not be breached... without explicit consent' is the conditional breach -> consent. CBTRN02C's 1500-B-LOOKUP-ACCT makes the antecedent always false (no transaction that would breach the limit is ever posted, lines 403-411 reject it via WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON=102, and the main loop never posts a failed transaction, lines 211-216), which satisfies the conditional regardless of whether a distinct consent mechanism exists. The cited text conditions breach on consent; it does not separately mandate that a consent-gated override path be offered. Pass 1's reading is accepted.

regulation_clause.text: The sanctioned credit limit shall not be breached at any point in time without explicit consent from the cardholder.

gold.gold_rationale: Clause 12(5) conditions breach on explicit consent (breach -> consent). 1500-B-LOOKUP-ACCT rejects any transaction that would exceed ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT (lines 403-411) and the main loop never posts a failed transaction (lines 211-216), making the antecedent always false and the conditional vacuously satisfied, per the adjudication note.

provenance.annotator_notes: Adjudicated 2026-07-27: Pass 1 read the blanket rejection of over-limit transactions as conformant (D7); Pass 2 read the absent consent-capture path as a missing rule (D2). Resolved on the clause's own grammar: 'shall not be breached... without explicit consent' is the conditional breach -> consent. CBTRN02C's 1500-B-LOOKUP-ACCT makes the antecedent always false (no transaction that would breach the limit is ever posted, lines 403-411 reject it via WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON=102, and the main loop never posts a failed transaction, lines 211-216), which satisfies the conditional regardless of whether a distinct consent mechanism exists. The cited text conditions breach on consent; it does not separately mandate that a consent-gated override path be offered. Pass 1's reading is accepted.

This is decisive primary evidence within the same bundle, not external or historical evidence, so the needs_adjudication gap is resolved rather than defaulted to exclude.

regulation_clause.text: Explicit consent is required to adjust credit (from refund/failed/reversed transactions already paid for) beyond a cut-off of one percent of the credit limit or Rs 5000, whichever is lower; consent sought within 7 days of the credit; on cardholder request, reversal to the bank account within 3 working days.

finding.rationale: Clause 31 requires explicit consent for the specified credit adjustments above the lower of 1% of the credit limit and ₹5,000. The program computes 1% and caps it at 6000 in WSCUTOFF.cpy line 4, then selects ADJUST unless the refund exceeds that cutoff at REFADJ2.cbl lines 24–27. For credit limits above ₹500,000, this can allow an adjustment above ₹5,000 without consent, so the configured cutoff is too high.

trajectory.final_answer: The configured cap is 6000, while the cited clause sets the cutoff at the lower of 1% of the credit limit or ₹5,000. The program can therefore permit adjustments above ₹5,000 without consent for credit limits above ₹500,000.
